channel.title: The San Francisco Standard - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The San Francisco Standard (sfstandard.com)

item.title: The race for 4,000: Ant Edwards, Kon Knueppel, and the generation coming for Steph Curry
item.description: The Standard caught up with Edwards, Knueppel, and the 3-point king himself to talk about how untouchable his greatest milestones are.

item.title: Six figures for signatures? California ballot bounties have gone wild
item.description: Signatures to qualify ballot measures are fetching unprecedented prices in part because of the battle over the billionaire tax.

item.title: More power to Lurie? New ballot measure could give SF mayors bigger say in hiring
item.description: City Hall leaders are preparing charter amendments for the November election to increase mayoral control.

item.title: The budget wars begin. Plus: Rich congressional candidate splashes out
item.description: Also in today’s Power Play: Some 2024 mayoral campaigns oopsies.

item.title: ‘Engineer’ is so 2025. In AI land, everyone’s a ‘builder’ now
item.description: From Big Tech to startups, Silicon Valley has a new job title for people who use AI agents to turn ideas into products.

item.title: Oakland reveals plans for Alysa Liu celebration
item.description: The March 12 event for the Olympic gold medalist is free, but registration is required.

item.title: Ousted DHS chief Noem praises Lurie, says he works ‘very well’ with feds
item.description: “He probably doesn’t want me to talk about it a lot,” said Noem on Thursday at a conference. “We have great conversations and talk quite often.”

item.title: A Bernal baking star is joining the rising food scene in the Outer Sunset
item.description: The duo behind Black Jet Baking Co. is bringing sprinkles, sandos, and sweet nostalgia to the city’s brink.

item.title: Ikea’s struggling food hall is losing another restaurant
item.description: With Cheezy’s leaving Saluhall, only three vendors remain.

item.title: Airbnb sued San Francisco over a $120 million tax bill. It didn’t work
item.description: Critics claimed the legal dispute tied up funds for public services amid budget shortfalls.
